# neatHack build companion

Work only inside the user's current project and follow its existing instructions.
Read https://neatlogs.com/hackathon and https://luma.com/s5blr882 for published

requirements. If these pages are unavailable or a

judging weights, prizes, deadlines or submission links.

Every project must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. Record how each tool is used

agent, and use cfo.ai to plan its pricing, costs, revenue and runway. Include
the business plan in the submission and explain all three tools in the demo.

Record tests that actually ran and failures that remain. Link to sanitized,
shareable evidence only. Never include API keys, .env contents, personal data,
private traces, access tokens or customer information. Do not fabricate results.

Before a demo, summarize what works and how to reproduce it. Check the latest
published requirements with the builder. Never register, publish, deploy or submit

import json, urllib.request

env = {}
with open(r"C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SwapDesk\.env") as f:
    for line in f:
        line=line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        k,v=line.split("=",1)
        env[k.strip()]=v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")

api_key = env.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY","")
url = "https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp"

session_id = None

def rpc(payload, method_label):
    global session_id
    data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="POST")
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    req.add_header("Accept", "application/json, text/event-stream")
    req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")
    if session_id:
        req.add_header("Mcp-Session-Id", session_id)
    # MCP protocol version header
    req.add_header("MCP-Protocol-Version", "2024-11-05")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
        hdrs = {k.lower(): v for k,v in r.headers.items()}
        # capture session
        for k,v in r.headers.items():
            if k.lower() in ("mcp-session-id", "mcp_session_id"):
                session_id = v
                print(f"[session captured] {k}={v[:16]}...")
        body = r.read().decode(errors="replace")
        print(f"=== {method_label} status={r.status} ===")
        print(f"headers: {dict(r.headers)}")
        print(body[:12000])
        print(f"=== END {method_label} ===")
        return body

# 1. initialize (already done, but redo to get session)
rpc({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"manual","version":"1.0"}}}, "initialize")

# 2. notifications/initialized
try:
    rpc({"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}, "notifications/initialized")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"notify err (may be ok, 202 accepted with empty): {e}")

# 3. tools/list
rpc({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}, "tools/list")

import json, urllib.request

env = {}
with open(r"C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SwapDesk\.env") as f:
    for line in f:
        line=line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        k,v=line.split("=",1)
        env[k.strip()]=v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")

api_key = env.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY","")
url = "https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp"

def rpc(payload, label, session_id):
    data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="POST")
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    req.add_header("Accept", "application/json, text/event-stream")
    req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")
    req.add_header("Mcp-Session-Id", session_id)
    req.add_header("MCP-Protocol-Version", "2024-11-05")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
        body = r.read().decode(errors="replace")
        print(f"=== {label} ===")
        print(body[:12000])
        print(f"=== END {label} ===")
        return body

# fresh session
def new_session():
    data = json.dumps({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"manual","version":"1.0"}}}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="POST")
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    req.add_header("Accept", "application/json, text/event-stream")
    req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
        sid = r.headers.get("mcp-session-id")
        body = r.read().decode()
        print(f"init sid={sid} body={body[:500]}")
        # notify
        data2 = json.dumps({"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}).encode()
        req2 = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data2, method="POST")
        req2.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        req2.add_header("Accept", "application/json, text/event-stream")
        req2.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")
        req2.add_header("Mcp-Session-Id", sid)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req2, timeout=30) as r2:
                r2.read()
                print("notified")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"notify: {e}")
        return sid

import json, urllib.request, re

env = {}
with open(r"C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SwapDesk\.env") as f:
    for line in f:
        line=line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        k,v=line.split("=",1)
        env[k.strip()]=v.strip().strip('"').strip("'")

api_key = env.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY","")
url = "https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp"

def rpc_raw(payload, session_id):
    data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="POST")
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    req.add_header("Accept", "application/json, text/event-stream")
    req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")
    req.add_header("Mcp-Session-Id", session_id)
    req.add_header("MCP-Protocol-Version", "2024-11-05")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return r.read().decode(errors="replace")

def new_session():
    data = json.dumps({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"manual","version":"1.0"}}}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="POST")
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    req.add_header("Accept", "application/json, text/event-stream")
    req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
        sid = r.headers.get("mcp-session-id")
        r.read()
        data2 = json.dumps({"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}).encode()
        req2 = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data2, method="POST")
        req2.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        req2.add_header("Accept", "application/json, text/event-stream")
        req2.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {api_key}")
        req2.add_header("Mcp-Session-Id", sid)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req2, timeout=30) as r2:
            r2.read()
        return sid

def parse_mcp_text(body):
    m = re.search(r"^data:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$", body, re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL)
    if not m:
        return None
    outer = json.loads(m.group(1))
    if "error" in outer:
        print("RPC ERROR:", json.dumps(outer["error"], indent=2))
        return None
    txt = outer["result"]["content"][0]["text"]
    return txt

sid = new_session()
body = rpc_raw({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}, sid)
txt = parse_mcp_text(body)
# txt is JSON string of tools list? Actually tools/list returns result.tools not content? Wait earlier tools/list returned result.tools directly, not content. Our parse expects content. Need handle both.
# Re-parse outer
m = re.search(r"^data:\s*(\{.*\})\s*$", body, re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL)
outer = json.loads(m.group(1))
result = outer.get("result", {})
if "tools" in result:
    tools = result["tools"]
    print(f"TOOL_COUNT={len(tools)}")
    for t in tools:
        print(f"- {t.get('name')}: {t.get('description','')[:120]}")
    with open(r"C:\Users\DELL\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\tools.json","w") as f:
        json.dump(tools, f, indent=2)
else:
    print(txt[:10000])

# MCP servers

Add local and remote MCP tools.

You can add external tools to OpenCode using the *Model Context Protocol*, or MCP. OpenCode supports both local and remote servers.

Once added, MCP tools are automatically available to the LLM alongside built-in tools.

---

#### [Caveats](#caveats)

When you use an MCP server, it adds to the context. This can quickly add up if you have a lot of tools. So we recommend being careful with which MCP servers you use.

Tip

MCP servers add to your context, so you want to be careful with which ones you enable.

Certain MCP servers, like the GitHub MCP server, tend to add a lot of tokens and can easily exceed the context limit.

---

## [Enable](#enable)

You can define MCP servers in your [OpenCode Config](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/) under `mcp`. Add each MCP with a unique name. You can refer to that MCP by name when prompting the LLM.

opencode.jsonc

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "name-of-mcp-server": {      // ...      "enabled": true,    },    "name-of-other-mcp-server": {      // ...    },  },}
```

You can also disable a server by setting `enabled` to `false`. This is useful if you want to temporarily disable a server without removing it from your config.

---

### [Overriding remote defaults](#overriding-remote-defaults)

Organizations can provide default MCP servers via their `.well-known/opencode` endpoint. These servers may be disabled by default, allowing users to opt-in to the ones they need.

To enable a specific server from your organization’s remote config, add it to your local config with `enabled: true`:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "jira": {      "type": "remote",      "url": "https://jira.example.com/mcp",      "enabled": true    }  }}
```

Your local config values override the remote defaults. See [config precedence](/docs/config#precedence-order) for more details.

---

## [Local](#local)

Add local MCP servers using `type` to `"local"` within the MCP object.

opencode.jsonc

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "my-local-mcp-server": {      "type": "local",      // Or ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command"]      "command": ["npx", "-y", "my-mcp-command"],      "enabled": true,      "environment": {        "MY_ENV_VAR": "my_env_var_value",      },    },  },}
```

The command is how the local MCP server is started. You can also pass in a list of environment variables as well.

For example, here’s how you can add the test [`@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything) MCP server.

opencode.jsonc

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "mcp_everything": {      "type": "local",      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"],    },  },}
```

And to use it I can add `use the mcp_everything tool` to my prompts.

```
use the mcp_everything tool to add the number 3 and 4
```

---

#### [Options](#options)

Here are all the options for configuring a local MCP server.

Option

Type

Required

Description

`type`

String

Y

Type of MCP server connection, must be `"local"`.

`command`

Array

Y

Command and arguments to run the MCP server.

`cwd`

String

Working directory for the MCP server process. Relative paths resolve from the workspace.

`environment`

Object

Environment variables to set when running the server.

`enabled`

Boolean

Enable or disable the MCP server on startup.

`timeout`

Number

Timeout in ms for fetching tools from the MCP server. Defaults to 5000 (5 seconds).

---

## [Remote](#remote)

Add remote MCP servers by setting `type` to `"remote"`.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "my-remote-mcp": {      "type": "remote",      "url": "https://my-mcp-server.com",      "enabled": true,      "headers": {        "Authorization": "Bearer MY_API_KEY"      }    }  }}
```

The `url` is the URL of the remote MCP server and with the `headers` option you can pass in a list of headers.

---

Option

`url`

---

## [OAuth](#oauth)

OpenCode automatically handles OAuth authentication for remote MCP servers. When a server requires authentication, OpenCode will:

1.  Detect the 401 response and initiate the OAuth flow
2.  Use **Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591)** if supported by the server
3.  Store tokens securely for future requests

---

### [Automatic](#automatic)

For most OAuth-enabled MCP servers, no special configuration is needed. Just configure the remote server:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "my-oauth-server": {      "type": "remote",      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp"    }  }}
```

If the server requires authentication, OpenCode will prompt you to authenticate when you first try to use it. If not, you can [manually trigger the flow](#authenticating) with `opencode mcp auth <server-name>`.

---

### [Pre-registered](#pre-registered)

If you have client credentials from the MCP server provider, you can configure them:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "my-oauth-server": {      "type": "remote",      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",      "oauth": {        "clientId": "{env:MY_MCP_CLIENT_ID}",        "clientSecret": "{env:MY_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET}",        "scope": "tools:read tools:execute"      }    }  }}
```

---

### [Authenticating](#authenticating)

You can manually trigger authentication or manage credentials.

Authenticate with a specific MCP server:

Terminal window

```
opencode mcp auth my-oauth-server
```

List all MCP servers and their auth status:

Terminal window

```
opencode mcp list
```

Remove stored credentials:

Terminal window

```
opencode mcp logout my-oauth-server
```

The `mcp auth` command will open your browser for authorization. After you authorize, OpenCode will store the tokens securely in `~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json`.

---

#### [Disabling OAuth](#disabling-oauth)

If you want to disable automatic OAuth for a server (e.g., for servers that use API keys instead), set `oauth` to `false`:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "my-api-key-server": {      "type": "remote",      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",      "oauth": false,      "headers": {        "Authorization": "Bearer {env:MY_API_KEY}"      }    }  }}
```

---

#### [OAuth Options](#oauth-options)

Option

Type

Description

`oauth`

Object | false

OAuth config object, or `false` to disable OAuth auto-detection.

`clientId`

String

OAuth client ID. If not provided, dynamic client registration will be attempted.

`clientSecret`

String

OAuth client secret, if required by the authorization server.

`scope`

String

OAuth scopes to request during authorization.

#### [Debugging](#debugging)

If a remote MCP server is failing to authenticate, you can diagnose issues with:

Terminal window

```
# View auth status for all OAuth-capable serversopencode mcp auth list
# Debug connection and OAuth flow for a specific serveropencode mcp debug my-oauth-server
```

The `mcp debug` command shows the current auth status, tests HTTP connectivity, and attempts the OAuth discovery flow.

---

## [Manage](#manage)

Tools from your MCP servers are available in OpenCode alongside built-in tools. You can manage them through the OpenCode config like any other tool.

---

### [Global](#global)

This means that you can enable or disable them globally.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "my-mcp-foo": {      "type": "local",      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command-foo"]    },    "my-mcp-bar": {      "type": "local",      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command-bar"]    }  },  "tools": {    "my-mcp-foo": false  }}
```

We can also use a glob pattern to disable all matching MCP tools.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "my-mcp-foo": {      "type": "local",      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command-foo"]    },    "my-mcp-bar": {      "type": "local",      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command-bar"]    }  },  "tools": {    "my-mcp*": false  }}
```

Here we are using the glob pattern `my-mcp*` to disable all matching MCP tools.

---

### [Per agent](#per-agent)

If you have a large number of MCP servers you may want to only enable them per agent and disable them globally. To do this:

1.  Disable it as a tool globally.
2.  In your [agent config](/docs/agents#tools), enable the MCP server as a tool.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "my-mcp": {      "type": "local",      "command": ["bun", "x", "my-mcp-command"],      "enabled": true    }  },  "tools": {    "my-mcp*": false  },  "agent": {    "my-agent": {      "tools": {        "my-mcp*": true      }    }  }}
```

---

#### [Glob patterns](#glob-patterns)

The glob pattern uses simple regex globbing patterns:

-   `*` matches zero or more of any character (e.g., `"my-mcp*"` matches `my-mcp_search`, `my-mcp_list`, etc.)
-   `?` matches exactly one character
-   All other characters match literally

Note

MCP server tools are registered with server name as prefix, so to disable all tools for a server simply use:

```
"mymcpservername_*": false
```

---

## [Examples](#examples)

Below are examples of some common MCP servers. You can submit a PR if you want to document other servers.

---

### [Sentry](#sentry)

Add the [Sentry MCP server](https://mcp.sentry.dev) to interact with your Sentry projects and issues.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "sentry": {      "type": "remote",      "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp",      "oauth": {}    }  }}
```

After adding the configuration, authenticate with Sentry:

Terminal window

```
opencode mcp auth sentry
```

This will open a browser window to complete the OAuth flow and connect OpenCode to your Sentry account.

Once authenticated, you can use Sentry tools in your prompts to query issues, projects, and error data.

```
Show me the latest unresolved issues in my project. use sentry
```

---

### [Context7](#context7)

Add the [Context7 MCP server](https://github.com/upstash/context7) to search through docs.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "context7": {      "type": "remote",      "url": "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp"    }  }}
```

If you have signed up for a free account, you can use your API key and get higher rate-limits.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "context7": {      "type": "remote",      "url": "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp",      "headers": {        "CONTEXT7_API_KEY": "{env:CONTEXT7_API_KEY}"      }    }  }}
```

Here we are assuming that you have the `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` environment variable set.

Add `use context7` to your prompts to use Context7 MCP server.

```
Configure a Cloudflare Worker script to cache JSON API responses for five minutes. use context7
```

Alternatively, you can add something like this to your [AGENTS.md](/docs/rules/).

AGENTS.md

```
When you need to search docs, use `context7` tools.
```

---

### [Grep by Vercel](#grep-by-vercel)

Add the [Grep by Vercel](https://grep.app) MCP server to search through code snippets on GitHub.

opencode.json

{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {    "gh_grep": {      "type": "remote",      "url": "https://mcp.grep.app"    }  }}
```

Since we named our MCP server `gh_grep`, you can add `use the gh_grep tool` to your prompts to get the agent to use it.

```
What's the right way to set a custom domain in an SST Astro component? use the gh_grep tool
```

Alternatively, you can add something like this to your [AGENTS.md](/docs/rules/).

AGENTS.md

```
If you are unsure how to do something, use `gh_grep` to search code examples from GitHub.
```

Highlights:
Neatlogs exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so your coding agent can read your observability data directly — search traces, pull the full context of a failing run, check detections, and act on fix suggestions — without you copying anything out of the dashboard.
...
The easiest way is the wizard, which offers to wire the MCP server into Claude Code or Cursor at the end of its run, or on its own:
...
To connect manually, add a `neatlogs` entry to your client's MCP config. The server speaks Streamable HTTP and authenticates with your project API key as a bearer token:
...
```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "neatlogs": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_PROJECT_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
...
The config file depends on your client — for example `.mcp.json` for Claude Code or `.cursor/mcp.json` for Cursor. The MCP server lives at `/mcp` on the same host as your SDK endpoint (the hosted default is `https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`; use your own host's `/mcp` if you self-host). Running `npx @neatlogs/wizard` wires this up for you.
...
The wizard merges ... other MCP servers
...
Once connected, the agent has tools to read and act on your Neatlogs data:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `search_traces` | Search traces by free-text query (BM25 keyword by default, or semantic vector search) |
| `get_trace_context` | Pull a trace's full context — metrics, span tree with inputs/outputs and code locations, and the detections that fired |
| `list_detections` | List the active detections enabled on the project |
| `get_detection_trend` | Get hourly / daily / weekly occurrence counts for a single detection |
| `triage_list` | List the current fix suggestions |
| `triage_get` | Get the full detail of one fix — root cause and recommended action |
| `triage_get_investigation` | Read the investigation that produced a fix — the root-cause reasoning trail |
| `triage_list_steps` | List the steps of an investigation thread |
| `triage_accept` / `triage_dismiss` / `triage_update_status` / `triage_update` | Act on a fix — accept, dismiss, move across the board, or update it |
| `log_trace` | Push a trace from your coding agent into Neatlogs |
| `ping` / `whoami` | Health check and identify the project this MCP session is bound to |

Title: MCP Integration
URL: https://docs.neatlogs.com/guides/mcp-integration
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
Connect AI agents and IDEs to Neatlogs via the Model Context Protocol. Query traces, manage fixes, and integrate observability into your workflows.

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard that allows AI agents and IDEs to interact with external systems through a unified tool interface. Neatlogs exposes a complete MCP server that lets Claude, coding agents, and IDE plugins access observability data, search traces, and manage fixes directly from your agent workflows.
...
Each Neatlogs project has its own API key. Go to Settings → API Keys in the dashboard, pick your project, and copy its key.
...
The fastest path is the wizard, which wires the MCP server into Claude Code or Cursor for you:
...
To connect manually, add a `neatlogs` entry to your client's MCP config (`.mcp.json` for Claude Code, `.cursor/mcp.json` for Cursor):
...
```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "neatlogs": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_PROJECT_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The MCP server lives at `/mcp` on the same host as your SDK endpoint — `https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp` on hosted Neatlogs, or your own host's `/mcp` if you self-host.

Authentication: Include the key in either header:

- `Authorization: Bearer ` (preferred — what most MCP clients send)
- `x-api-key: ` (legacy, still accepted)
...
Restart your editor and the Neatlogs tools appear in your agent's tool list. Ask the agent to call `ping` to verify the connection, and `whoami` to confirm which project the session is bound to. From there it can call any tool — for example, search traces for a specific error.

## Connection Methods

HTTP Streamable (Recommended) SSE Streaming (Legacy)
...
Stateful sessions that you can reuse for multiple requests. The first `initialize` request creates a session; the server returns its id in the `mcp-session-id` response header.
...
```
POST https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp
Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "initialize",
  "params": {
    "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
    "capabilities": {},
    "clientInfo": { "name": "my-agent", "version": "1.0" }
  }
}
...
Then call tools on the session, passing the id back in the `mcp-session-id` header:
...
```
POST https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp
Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream
mcp-session-id: <session-id-from-initialize>

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "search_traces",
    "arguments": {
      "query": "timeout"
    }
  }
}
...
- Stateful sessions (reuse connections)
- Include `mcp-session-id` header to resume
- GET, POST, DELETE supported
- Rate limited: 60 requests/minute
- Best for agents and IDEs
...
Event-based streaming with persistent connections.
...
```
GET https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp/sse
Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>

# Connection opens, receives events
# Then POST messages to:
POST https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp/messages?sessionId=<session-id>
...
- Server-sent events (SSE)
- Keep connection alive for streaming
- The GET stream is not rate-limited (won't break long-lived connections)

### Bearer Token (Standard)
...
```
Authorization: Bearer <your-project-api-key>
...
### Legacy Header (x-api-key)
...
```
x-api-key: <your-project-api-key>
...
API keys are unique per project. Each key grants access to one project only — the session sees only that project's traces, detections, and fixes.

### Creating a Session

The `initialize` request creates a new session:
...
```
POST https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp
Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>
...
The server returns the session id in the `mcp-session-id` response header. Store this for subsequent calls.

### Resuming a Session

Reuse an existing session by including the header:
...
```
POST https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp
Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>
mcp-session-id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
...
Same session, same tools advertised, same context. Sessions are bound to the project that created them — reusing a session id with a different project's key returns `403`.

### Cleaning Up

Send DELETE to tear down a session:
...
```
DELETE https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp
Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>
mcp-session-id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
...
cleaned up when the
...
## Rate Limiting

- Limit: 60 requests per 60 seconds
- Applies to: POST and DELETE only
- Excludes: GET (SSE streaming) to avoid breaking long-lived connections
- Response: 429 Too Many Requests if exceeded
...
## Tool Overview

| Tool | Purpose | Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ping | Health check | Verify connection |
| whoami | Get project ID | Confirm authentication |
| search_traces | Keyword or semantic search | Find errors, slow or expensive traces |
| get_trace_context | Fetch span tree | View execution details |
| list_detections | List active detections | See what's being monitored |
| get_detection_trend | Trend analysis | Track detection frequency |
| log_trace | Push traces | Agent reports its work |
| triage_list | List fixes | See all suggestions |
| triage_get | Fix details | Review root cause + action |
| triage_get_investigation | Investigation context | Read investigation thread |
| triage_list_steps | Investigation steps | See agent's analysis steps |
| triage_list_versions | List fix versions | Browse saved content versions of a fix |
| triage_get_version | Fetch fix version | Read one version snapshot by number |
| triage_restore_version | Restore fix version | Roll a fix's content back to an older version |
| triage_accept | Accept fix | Move to Kanban board |
| triage_dismiss | Reject fix | Mark as false positive |
| triage_update_status | Change status | Move across `in_progress` / `resolved` / `archived` |
| triage_update | Edit fix fields | Update title, severity, label, action |

See the MCP Tools Reference for detailed schemas and examples.
...
### Authentication Errors

| Status | Reason | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | Missing API key | Include Authorization header |
| 401 | Invalid API key | Check the key against Settings → API Keys |
| 403 | Session belongs to different project | Use the same project's API key for the session |
...
| Missing ` ... -session- ... DELETE | Include
...
All error responses include an `error` field with details. Calling a tool that isn't enabled returns a JSON-RPC error — disabled tools are never advertised in `tools/list`, so a well-behaved client won't hit this.
...
### "API key required"

Missing or malformed Authorization header. Ensure the header is present and the format is correct.
...
Key doesn't match any project. Copy ... Settings → API Keys.
...
### "Session not found" / "Unknown sessionId"

Session was torn down or the connection closed. Initialize a new session (omit the `mcp-session-id` header on the next `initialize`).
...
### A tool is missing from `tools/list`

On self-hosted deployments, tools are enabled per-deployment in the backend `tools.yaml`. On hosted Neatlogs, all current tools are enabled — update your client if it's pinned to an old tool list.

Highlights:
Connect your own apps — GitHub, Linear, Slack, Notion and more — so Copilot and Neat Agent can use them on your behalf.

When you're debugging an agent, the context you need is rarely all in Neatlogs. The failing run points at a pull request, a Linear issue, a Slack thread, or a Notion doc. Tools & MCPs lets you connect those accounts to Neatlogs so Copilot and Neat Agent can read from — and act in — them while they help you, without you leaving the chat to go copy things across.

You connect apps under Settings → Tools & MCPs, and each teammate connects their own accounts. Tools always run with your permissions — Copilot only ever sees the repos, issues, and channels you can, never a shared team token.
...
Connect any of these with a single OAuth sign-in — no tokens to paste, no configuration:

| App | What Copilot & Neat Agent can do |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub | Search your code and read repository files to ground a fix in the actual source |
| Linear | Look up and read issues so a run can be tied back to the ticket that tracks it |
| Slack | Read channel history for context, and post updates back to your team |
| Notion | Search and read pages and docs from your knowledge base |

These four are featured, but the catalog is larger — search Settings → Tools & MCPs for others (for example Gmail or Jira). Apps that aren't available yet appear as Coming soon.
...
1. Open Settings → Tools & MCPs.
2. Find the app — apps are grouped into Connected, Featured, and All apps, with a search box.
3. Toggle it on. You're sent to that app's sign-in page to authorize Neatlogs.
4. On return, the card shows a Connected for you badge. That's it — the app is now available in chat.
...
### Custom MCP servers

Already run your own Model Context Protocol server? Add it under Settings → Tools & MCPs → Add MCP server by giving it a name and an `https` URL, plus any auth headers it needs. A Test button checks the connection before you save.

Custom MCP servers power Neatlogs' evaluators — an AI judge can call your own tools while scoring runs. The featured OAuth apps above are what Copilot and Neat Agent use in chat.
...
Neatlogs has two places to connect outside tools, for two different jobs:

| | Tools & MCPs | Integrations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Purpose | Give Copilot & Neat Agent tools to use in chat | Wire Neatlogs into your workflow — alerts, issue creation, trace import |
| Connected by | Each teammate, individually | Set up once for the workspace |
| Examples | GitHub, Linear, Slack, Notion for chat context | Slack alert routing, creating a Linear issue from a detection, importing traces |

Some of the same apps appear in both — that's expected. In Tools & MCPs they're tools you wield through chat; in Integrations they're wired into automated Neatlogs workflows.

# Permissions

Control which actions require approval to run.

OpenCode uses the `permission` config to decide whether a given action should run automatically, prompt you, or be blocked.

As of `v1.1.1`, the legacy `tools` boolean config is deprecated and has been merged into `permission`. The old `tools` config is still supported for backwards compatibility.

---

## [Actions](#actions)

Each permission rule resolves to one of:

-   `"allow"` — run without approval
-   `"ask"` — prompt for approval
-   `"deny"` — block the action

---

## [Auto mode](#auto-mode)

Start OpenCode with `--auto` to automatically approve permission requests that are not explicitly denied.

Terminal window

```
opencode --auto
```

You can also use auto mode with [`opencode run`](/docs/cli#run).

Terminal window

```
opencode run --auto "Refactor this module"
```

Explicit `"deny"` rules are still enforced. Auto mode only changes requests that would otherwise ask for approval.

In the TUI, open the command palette and select **Enable auto-approve permissions** or **Disable auto-approve permissions** to change modes. When auto mode is active, the prompt displays a muted `auto` indicator next to the current agent.

---

## [Configuration](#configuration)

You can set permissions globally (with `*`), and override specific tools.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "permission": {    "*": "ask",    "bash": "allow",    "edit": "deny"  }}
```

You can also set all permissions at once:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "permission": "allow"}
```

---

## [Granular Rules (Object Syntax)](#granular-rules-object-syntax)

For most permissions, you can use an object to apply different actions based on the tool input.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "permission": {    "bash": {      "*": "ask",      "git *": "allow",      "npm *": "allow",      "rm *": "deny",      "grep *": "allow"    },    "edit": {      "*": "deny",      "packages/web/src/content/docs/*.mdx": "allow"    },    "webfetch": {      "*": "ask",      "https://en.wikipedia.org/*": "allow"    }  }}
```

Rules are evaluated by pattern match, with the **last matching rule winning**. A common pattern is to put the catch-all `"*"` rule first, and more specific rules after it.

### [Wildcards](#wildcards)

Permission patterns use simple wildcard matching:

-   `*` matches zero or more of any character
-   `?` matches exactly one character
-   All other characters match literally

### [Home Directory Expansion](#home-directory-expansion)

You can use `~` or `$HOME` at the start of a pattern to reference your home directory. This is particularly useful for [`external_directory`](#external-directories) rules.

-   `~/projects/*` -> `/Users/username/projects/*`
-   `$HOME/projects/*` -> `/Users/username/projects/*`
-   `~` -> `/Users/username`

### [External Directories](#external-directories)

Use `external_directory` to allow tool calls that touch paths outside the working directory where OpenCode was started. This applies to any tool that takes a path as input (for example `read`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, and many `bash` commands).

Home expansion (like `~/...`) only affects how a pattern is written. It does not make an external path part of the current workspace, so paths outside the working directory must still be allowed via `external_directory`.

For example, this allows access to everything under `~/projects/personal/`:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "permission": {    "external_directory": {      "~/projects/personal/**": "allow"    }  }}
```

Any directory allowed here inherits the same defaults as the current workspace. Since [`read` defaults to `allow`](#defaults), reads are also allowed for entries under `external_directory` unless overridden. Add explicit rules when a tool should be restricted in these paths, such as blocking edits while keeping reads:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "permission": {    "external_directory": {      "~/projects/personal/**": "allow"    },    "edit": {      "~/projects/personal/**": "deny"    }  }}
```

Keep the list focused on trusted paths, and layer extra allow or deny rules as needed for other tools (for example `bash`).

---

## [Available Permissions](#available-permissions)

OpenCode permissions are keyed by tool name, plus a couple of safety guards:

-   `read` — reading a file (matches the file path)
-   `edit` — all file modifications (covers `edit`, `write`, `patch`)
-   `glob` — file globbing (matches the glob pattern)
-   `grep` — content search (matches the regex pattern)
-   `bash` — running shell commands (matches parsed commands like `git status --porcelain`)
-   `task` — launching subagents (matches the subagent type)
-   `skill` — loading a skill (matches the skill name)
-   `lsp` — running LSP queries (currently non-granular)
-   `question` — asking the user questions during execution
-   `webfetch` — fetching a URL (matches the URL)
-   `websearch` — web search
-   `external_directory` — triggered when a tool touches paths outside the project working directory
-   `doom_loop` — triggered when the same tool call repeats 3 times with identical input

---

## [Defaults](#defaults)

If you don’t specify anything, OpenCode starts from permissive defaults:

-   Most permissions default to `"allow"`.
-   `doom_loop` and `external_directory` default to `"ask"`.
-   `read` is `"allow"`, but `.env` files are denied by default:

opencode.json

```
{  "permission": {    "read": {      "*": "allow",      "*.env": "deny",      "*.env.*": "deny",      "*.env.example": "allow"    }  }}
```

---

## [What “Ask” Does](#what-ask-does)

When OpenCode prompts for approval, the UI offers three outcomes:

-   `once` — approve just this request
-   `always` — approve future requests matching the suggested patterns (for the rest of the current OpenCode session)
-   `reject` — deny the request

The set of patterns that `always` would approve is provided by the tool (for example, bash approvals typically whitelist a safe command prefix like `git status*`).

---

## [Agents](#agents)

You can override permissions per agent. Agent permissions are merged with the global config, and agent rules take precedence. [Learn more](/docs/agents#permissions) about agent permissions.

Note

Refer to the [Granular Rules (Object Syntax)](#granular-rules-object-syntax) section above for more detailed pattern matching examples.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "permission": {    "bash": {      "*": "ask",      "git *": "allow",      "git commit *": "deny",      "git push *": "deny",      "grep *": "allow"    }  },  "agent": {    "build": {      "permission": {        "bash": {          "*": "ask",          "git *": "allow",          "git commit *": "ask",          "git push *": "deny",          "grep *": "allow"        }      }    }  }}
```

You can also configure agent permissions in Markdown:

~/.config/opencode/agents/review.md

```
---description: Code review without editsmode: subagentpermission:  edit: deny  bash: ask  webfetch: deny---
Only analyze code and suggest changes.
```

Tip

Use pattern matching for commands with arguments. `"grep *"` allows `grep pattern file.txt`, while `"grep"` alone would block it. Commands like `git status` work for default behavior but require explicit permission (like `"git status *"`) when arguments are passed.

    data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="POST")
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")

        return r.read().decode(errors="replace")

286: def continue_case(db_path, *, case_id: str, message: str = "",
287:                   consent_size: str | None = None,

290:                   size: str | None = None, qty: int = 1) -> dict:
291:     """Continue a case with new customer input.

294:     request runs again under a fresh run id (duplicate-safe). The request
295:     comes from explicit fields when given, else from the case's latest
296:     exchange row; without either, continuation is a client error.
297:     """

300:     if current["outcome"] in ("arranged", "denial"):
301:         return {"case_id": case_id, "run_id": None, **current,
302:                 "attempts": {}, "continued": False}

319:                 "provide order_id, order_item_id and size")
320:         request = dict(anchor)

1: """Deterministic reference driver. NOT the agent.
2: 
3: Follows one fixed, documented policy so the checker has real executions
4: to verify against the frozen cases. The Slice 4 agent will face the same
5: cases without ever seeing expected answers.
6: 
7: Policy: unknown/mismatched item -> clarification; ineligible -> denial;
8: missing size -> clarification; insufficient stock -> consented alternative
9: or clarification; faults -> bounded retries on the SAME key (re-query
10: status after crash/timeout); exhausted retries or abandonment ->
11: escalation with release. Replies are fixed templates (a preview of the
12: Slice 4 verified-template rule), never model prose.
13: """
14: 
15: from __future__ import annotations
16: 
17: from datetime import date
18: 
19: from swapdesk import (
20:     InsufficientStockError,
21:     LabelTimeoutError,
22:     OperationError,
23:     ReleaseFailedError,
24:     TransientError,
25:     WorkerCrashedError,
26:     cancel_exchange,
27:     create_label,
28:     create_return,
29:     escalate_case,
30:     finalize_arranged,
31:     find_exchange_stock,
32:     note_case,
33:     reserve_replacement,
34: )

36: from swapdesk.models import OrderItem
37: from swapdesk.policy import check_eligibility
38: 
39: MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
40: 
41: 
42: def _record(row) -> OrderItem:
43:     return OrderItem(
44:         id=row["id"], order_id=row["order_id"], sku=row["sku"],
45:         size=row["size"], qty=row["qty"], price_cents=row["price_cents"],
46:         status=row["status"], delivered_at=row["delivered_at"],
47:         final_sale=bool(row["final_sale"]), created_at=row["created_at"],
48:     )

51: def _pool(db_path, sku: str, size: str):
52:     conn = connect(db_path)
53:     try:
54:         return find_exchange_stock(conn, sku, size)
55:     finally:
56:         conn.close()
57:

59: class _Exhausted(Exception):
60:     pass
61: 
62: 
63: def _key(case_id: str, run_tag: str, step: str) -> str:
64:     return f"{case_id}:{run_tag}:{step}"
65: 
66: 
67: def _deny(db_path, case_id: str, reason: str) -> dict:
68:     note_case(db_path, case_id=case_id, state="denied", detail=reason)
69:     return {"case_id": case_id, "outcome": "denied", "exchange_id": None,
70:             "status": None, "reason": f"denied: {reason}", "question": None,
71:             "duplicate": False, "attempts": {}}
72: 
73: 
74: def _clarify(db_path, case_id: str, question: str) -> dict:
75:     note_case(db_path, case_id=case_id, state="needs_information",
76:               detail=question)
77:     return {"case_id": case_id, "outcome": "clarification",
78:             "exchange_id": None, "status": None, "reason": None,
79:             "question": f"clarification: {question}", "duplicate": False,
80:             "attempts": {}}
81:

83: def _attempt(log: dict, step: str, fn):
84:     """Bounded retries on the same key. Crash/timeout recover via saved."""
85:     last = None
86:     for n in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
87:         log["attempts"][step] = n
88:         try:
89:             return fn()
90:         except (TransientError, WorkerCrashedError, LabelTimeoutError,
91:                 InsufficientStockError) as exc:
92:             last = exc
93:     raise _Exhausted(str(last))
94: 
95: 
96: def _escalate_none(db_path, case_id: str, reason: str) -> dict:
97:     note_case(db_path, case_id=case_id, state="escalated", detail=reason)
98:     return {"case_id": case_id, "outcome": "escalated", "exchange_id": None,
99:             "status": None, "reason": f"escalated: {reason}",
100:             "question": None, "duplicate": False, "attempts": {}}

103: def _escalate_held(db_path, case_id: str, run_id: str, op_key: str,
104:                    exchange_id: str, reason: str, log: dict) -> dict:
105:     last = None
106:     for n in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
107:         log["attempts"]["escalate"] = n
108:         try:
109:             out = escalate_case(db_path, case_id=case_id, run_id=run_id,
110:                                 op_key=op_key, exchange_id=exchange_id,
111:                                 reason=reason)
112:             return {"case_id": case_id, "outcome": "escalated",
113:                     "exchange_id": exchange_id, "status": out.status,
114:                     "reason": f"escalated: {reason}", "question": None,
115:                     "duplicate": out.duplicate, "attempts": log["attempts"]}
116:         except (ReleaseFailedError, TransientError) as exc:
117:             last = exc
118:     return {"case_id": case_id, "outcome": "escalated",
119:             "exchange_id": exchange_id, "status": "cleanup_pending",
120:             "reason": f"escalated: {reason} (cleanup pending: {last})",
121:             "question": None, "duplicate": False, "attempts": log["attempts"]}

124: def _fetch_item(db_path, order_item_id: str):
125:     conn = connect(db_path)
126:     try:
127:         return conn.execute("SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE id = ?",
128:                             (order_item_id,)).fetchone()
129:     finally:
130:         conn.close()

133: def _run_standard(db_path, case: dict, run_tag: str = "r1",
134:                   case_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
135:     cid = case_id or case["case_id"]
136:     run_id = case.get("run_id", f"{cid}-RUN-{run_tag}")
137:     log: dict = {"case_id": cid, "outcome": None, "exchange_id": None,
138:                  "status": None, "reason": None, "question": None,
139:                  "duplicate": False, "attempts": {}}
140:     qty = case.get("qty", 1)
141: 
142:     row = _fetch_item(db_path, case["order_item_id"])
143:     if row is None:
144:         return _clarify(db_path, cid,
145:                         "provide your order number and item id")
146:     if row["order_id"] != case["order_id"]:
147:         return _clarify(
148:             db_path, cid,
149:             f"item {case['order_item_id']} is not on order "
150:             f"{case['order_id']}; check both and reply")
151:     item = dict(row)
152:     eligible, reason = check_eligibility(_record(row), date.today())
153:     if not eligible:
154:         return _deny(db_path, cid, reason)
155: 
156:     size = (case.get("requested_size") or "").strip()
157:     if not size:
158:         return _clarify(db_path, cid, "which size do you need?")
159:     pool = _pool(db_path, item["sku"], size)
160:     available = pool.available if pool else 0
161:     authorized = size
162:     if available < qty:
163:         consent = case.get("consent_size")
164:         if consent:
165:             alt = _pool(db_path, item["sku"], consent)
166:             if alt is not None and alt.available >= qty:
167:                 authorized = consent
168:                 note_case(db_path, case_id=cid, state="received",
169:                           detail=f"consent:{consent}")
170:         if authorized == size:
171:             return _clarify(
172:                 db_path, cid,
173:                 f"size {size} is unavailable (only {available} unit(s) in "
174:                 "stock); reply with an alternative size or ask for a human")
175: 
176:     def do_reserve():
177:         return reserve_replacement(
178:             db_path, case_id=cid, run_id=run_id,
179:             op_key=_key(cid, run_tag, "reserve"),
180:             order_id=case["order_id"], order_item_id=case["order_item_id"],
181:             size=authorized, qty=qty, requested_size=size,
182:             consent=authorized != size)
183: 
184:     try:
185:         res = _attempt(log, "reserve", do_reserve)
186:     except _Exhausted as exc:
187:         return _escalate_none(db_path, cid, f"reservation kept failing: {exc}")
188:     except OperationError as exc:
189:         return _escalate_none(db_path, cid, f"reservation failed: {exc}")
190:     if res.duplicate and res.status == "arranged":
191:         log.update(outcome="arranged", exchange_id=res.exchange_id,
192:                    status="arranged", duplicate=True)
193:         return log
194:     exchange_id = res.exchange_id
195:     log["duplicate"] = res.duplicate
196: 
197:     if case.get("abandon_after") == "reserved":
198:         return _escalate_held(db_path, cid, run_id,
199:                               _key(cid, run_tag, "escalate"), exchange_id,
200:                               "customer abandonment", log)
201: 
202:     def do_return():
203:         return create_return(db_path, case_id=cid, run_id=run_id,
204:                              op_key=_key(cid, run_tag, "return"),
205:                              exchange_id=exchange_id)
206: 
207:     def do_label():
208:         return create_label(db_path, case_id=cid, run_id=run_id,
209:                             op_key=_key(cid, run_tag, "label"),
210:                             exchange_id=exchange_id)
211: 
212:     def do_finalize():
213:         return finalize_arranged(db_path, case_id=cid, run_id=run_id,
214:                                  op_key=_key(cid, run_tag, "finalize"),
215:                                  exchange_id=exchange_id)
216: 
217:     try:
218:         _attempt(log, "return", do_return)
219:         if case.get("abandon_after") == "return_created":
220:             return _escalate_held(db_path, cid, run_id,
221:                                   _key(cid, run_tag, "escalate"), exchange_id,
222:                                   "customer abandonment", log)
223:         _attempt(log, "label", do_label)
224:         if case.get("abandon_after") == "label_created":
225:             return _escalate_held(db_path, cid, run_id,
226:                                   _key(cid, run_tag, "escalate"), exchange_id,
227:                                   "customer abandonment", log)
228:         _attempt(log, "finalize", do_finalize)
229:     except _Exhausted as exc:
230:         return _escalate_held(db_path, cid, run_id,
231:                               _key(cid, run_tag, "escalate"), exchange_id,
232:                               f"flow kept failing: {exc}", log)
233:     except OperationError as exc:
234:         return _escalate_held(db_path, cid, run_id,
235:                               _key(cid, run_tag, "escalate"), exchange_id,
236:                               f"flow failed: {exc}", log)
237:     log.update(outcome="arranged", exchange_id=exchange_id,
238:                status="arranged")
239:     return log

242: def run_case(db_path, case: dict, run_tag: str = "r1") -> dict:
243:     """Run one frozen case by script name. Scripts share one database."""
244:     script = case.get("script", "standard")
245:     if script == "standard":
246:         if case.get("split_runs"):
247:             return _run_split(db_path, case, run_tag)
248:         return _run_standard(db_path, case, run_tag)
249:     if script == "rerun":
250:         first = _run_standard(db_path, case, "r1")
251:         second = _run_standard(db_path, case, "r2")
252:         first["second"] = second
253:         first["duplicate"] = second.get("duplicate", False)
254:         first["status"] = second.get("status", first.get("status"))
255:         return first
256:     if script == "cross_case":
257:         first = _run_standard(db_path, case, "r1")
258:         second_case = dict(case["second_case"])
259:         second = _run_standard(db_path, second_case, "r1",
260:                                case_id=second_case["case_id"])
261:         first["second"] = second
262:         first["duplicate"] = second.get("duplicate", False)
263:         return first
264:     if script == "cancel_fresh":
265:         first = _run_standard(db_path, case, "r1")
266:         cancel_exchange(db_path, case_id=case["case_id"],
267:                         run_id=f"{case['case_id']}-RUN-r1x",
268:                         op_key=f"{case['case_id']}:r1x:cancel",
269:                         exchange_id=first["exchange_id"],
270:                         reason="customer changed mind, retrying fresh")
271:         second = _run_standard(db_path, case, "r2")
272:         second["first_exchange"] = first["exchange_id"]
273:         return second
274:     raise ValueError(f"unknown script {script!r}")
275: 
276: 
277: def _run_split(db_path, case: dict, run_tag: str) -> dict:
278:     """Reserve under RUN-1, finish under RUN-2: progress spans runs."""
279:     cid = case["case_id"]
280:     res = reserve_replacement(
281:         db_path, case_id=cid, run_id=f"{cid}-RUN-1",
282:         op_key=_key(cid, run_tag, "reserve"), order_id=case["order_id"],
283:         order_item_id=case["order_item_id"], size=case["requested_size"],
284:         qty=case.get("qty", 1))
285:     create_return(db_path, case_id=cid, run_id=f"{cid}-RUN-2",

1: """Frozen-benchmark harness: fresh DB per run, faults armed, checked.
2: 
3: Each case run gets an isolated database so runs never interfere (except
4: scripts that intentionally share one DB within a single run). Results
5: carry case/version identifiers plus the observed outcome; expected
6: answers stay in the cases file, which the future agent never sees.
7: """
8: 
9: from __future__ import annotations
10: 
11: import json
12: import tempfile
13: from datetime import datetime, timezone
14: from pathlib import Path
15: 
16: from swapdesk import faults
17: from swapdesk.checker import check_run
18: from swapdesk.db import connect, init_db
19: from swapdesk.fixtures import load_fixtures
20: 
21: TABLES = ("orders", "order_items", "stock", "exchanges", "returns",
22:           "labels", "operations", "journal", "cases")
23: 
24: 
25: def fresh_db() -> Path:
26:     tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="swapdesk-eval-"))
27:     db_path = tmp / "shop.db"
28:     conn = connect(db_path)
29:     try:
30:         init_db(conn)
31:         load_fixtures(conn)
32:     finally:
33:         conn.close()
34:     return db_path
35: 
36: 
37: def snapshot(db_path) -> dict:
38:     conn = connect(db_path)
39:     try:
40:         return {t: [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {t}")]
41:                 for t in TABLES}
42:     finally:
43:         conn.close()
44: 
45: 
46: def _arm(case_id: str, run_tag: str, fault_specs: list) -> None:
47:     for spec in fault_specs:
48:         faults.inject(f"{case_id}:{run_tag}:{spec['step']}",
49:                       spec["point"], spec.get("times", 1))
50: 
51: 
52: def run_benchmark(cases: list[dict]) -> dict:
53:     from eval.driver import run_case
54:     runs = []
55:     for case in cases:
56:         for rep in range(1, case.get("repeats", 1) + 1):
57:             run_tag = f"r{rep}"
58:             db_path = fresh_db()
59:             baseline = snapshot(db_path)
60:             faults.clear()
61:             _arm(case["case_id"], run_tag, case.get("faults", []))
62:             second = case.get("second_case")
63:             if second:
64:                 _arm(second["case_id"], run_tag,
65:                      second.get("faults", []))
66:             try:
67:                 log = run_case(db_path, case, run_tag)
68:             finally:
69:                 faults.clear()
70:             check = check_run(db_path, case, log, baseline, repeat=rep)
71:             runs.append({
72:                 "benchmark_version": case.get("_version", "benchmark-v1"),
73:                 "case_id": case["case_id"],
74:                 "repeat": rep,
75:                 "passed": check.passed,
76:                 "failures": check.failures,
77:                 "observed": {
78:                     "outcome": log.get("outcome"),
79:                     "exchange_id": log.get("exchange_id"),
80:                     "status": log.get("status"),
81:                     "duplicate": log.get("duplicate", False),
82:                 },
83:             })
84:     passed = sum(1 for r in runs if r["passed"])
85:     return {
86:         "generated_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(
87:             timespec="seconds"),
88:         "total": len(runs),
89:         "passed": passed,
90:         "failed": len(runs) - passed,
91:         "runs": runs,
92:     }

1: """Deterministic benchmark checker. No LLM judge, no agent imports.
2: 
3: check_run() re-derives everything from the database plus a pre-run
4: baseline snapshot: expected outcome per case, global invariants
5: (nonnegative inventory, hold reconciliation, journal linkage, no
6: unrelated record changes), and run-log truthfulness (the driver must
7: not claim what the database does not show).
8: """
9: 
10: from __future__ import annotations
11: 
12: import sqlite3
13: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
14: from datetime import date
15: import json as _json
16: 
17: from .db import connect
18: from .operations import verify_exchange
19: from .policy import check_eligibility
20: 
21: 
22: @dataclass
23: class CheckResult:
24:     case_id: str
25:     repeat: int
26:     passed: bool
27:     failures: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
28: 
29: 
30: def _failures() -> list[str]:
31:     return []
32: 
33: 
34: def _rows(conn: sqlite3.Connection, table: str) -> list[dict]:
35:     return [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table}")]
36: 
37: 
38: def _snapshot(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict:
39:     return {
40:         "orders": _rows(conn, "orders"),
41:         "order_items": _rows(conn, "order_items"),
42:         "stock": _rows(conn, "stock"),
43:     }
44: 
45: 
46: def check_run(db_path, case: dict, run_log: dict, baseline: dict,
47:               repeat: int = 1) -> CheckResult:
48:     """Verify one case execution. Returns pass/fail with reasons."""
49:     failures = _failures()
50:     case_id = case["case_id"]
51:     outcome = case["outcome"]
52: 
53:     conn = connect(db_path)
54:     try:
55:         after = _snapshot(conn)
56:         exchanges = _rows(conn, "exchanges")
57:         returns = _rows(conn, "returns")
58:         labels = _rows(conn, "labels")
59:         operations = _rows(conn, "operations")
60:         journal = _rows(conn, "journal")
61:         cases = {}
62:         for r in _rows(conn, "cases"):
63:             row = dict(r)
64:             row["progress"] = _json.loads(row.pop("progress_json"))
65:             cases[row["case_id"]] = row
66:     finally:
67:         conn.close()
68: 
69:     item_id = case["order_item_id"]
70:     item_exchanges = [e for e in exchanges if e["order_item_id"] == item_id]
71:     case_ops = [o for o in operations
72:                 if o["case_id"] in _involved_cases(case, run_log)]
73: 
74:     _check_invariants(case, baseline, after, exchanges, operations, journal,
75:                       failures)
76:     _check_log_truthfulness(case, run_log, item_exchanges, failures)
77: 
78:     if outcome == "arranged":
79:         _check_arranged(db_path, case, run_log, item_exchanges, returns,
80:                         labels, case_ops, cases, baseline, after, failures)
81:     elif outcome in ("denied", "clarification"):
82:         _check_no_writes(case, run_log, item_exchanges, returns, labels,
83:                          case_ops, baseline, after, failures)
84:         _check_case_state(case, cases, failures)
85:         _check_message(case, run_log, failures)
86:     elif outcome == "escalated":
87:         _check_escalated(db_path, case, run_log, item_exchanges, returns,
88:                          labels, case_ops, cases, failures)
89:     else:
90:         failures.append(f"unknown expected outcome {outcome!r}")
91: 
92:     return CheckResult(case_id=case_id, repeat=repeat,
93:                        passed=not failures, failures=failures)
94: 
95: 
96: def _involved_cases(case: dict, run_log: dict) -> set[str]:
97:     ids = {case["case_id"]}
98:     second = run_log.get("second") or {}
99:     if second.get("case_id"):
100:         ids.add(second["case_id"])
101:     return ids
102: 
103: 
104: def _check_invariants(case, baseline, after, exchanges, operations, journal,
105:                       failures) -> None:
106:     # Orders and items are reference data: never change.
107:     if after["orders"] != baseline["orders"]:
108:         failures.append("orders table changed during the run")
109:     if after["order_items"] != baseline["order_items"]:
110:         failures.append("order_items table changed during the run")
111:     # Nonnegative inventory everywhere.
112:     for row in after["stock"]:
113:         if row["held"] < 0 or row["on_hand"] < 0:
114:             failures.append(
115:                 f"negative stock at {row['sku']}/{row['size']}")
116:         if row["on_hand"] - row["held"] < 0:
117:             failures.append(
118:                 f"oversold pool {row['sku']}/{row['size']}")
119:     # Hold reconciliation: every outstanding hold is backed by an exchange.
120:     held_total = sum(r["held"] for r in after["stock"])
121:     base_held = sum(r["held"] for r in baseline["stock"])
122:     open_holds = sum(
123:         e["qty"] for e in exchanges
124:         if not e["hold_released"] and e["status"] in (
125:             "replacement_reserved", "return_created", "label_created",
126:             "cleanup_pending"))
127:     if held_total != base_held + open_holds:
128:         failures.append(
129:             f"orphan holds: stock held={held_total} but open exchange "
130:             f"holds={open_holds} (baseline {base_held})")
131:     # Journal linkage: every recorded op key left at least one event.
132:     journaled = {j["op_key"] for j in journal}
133:     for op in operations:
134:         if op["idempotency_key"] not in journaled:
135:             failures.append(
136:                 f"op {op['idempotency_key']!r} has no journal event")
137:     # Only the case's own pools may move.
138:     allowed_pools = {(case.get("sku"), case.get("requested_size")),
139:                      (case.get("sku"), case.get("consent_size"))}
140:     before_pools = {(r["sku"], r["size"]): (r["on_hand"], r["held"])
141:                     for r in baseline["stock"]}
142:     after_pools = {(r["sku"], r["size"]): (r["on_hand"], r["held"])
143:                    for r in after["stock"]}
144:     for pool, vals in after_pools.items():
145:         if vals != before_pools.get(pool) and pool not in allowed_pools:
146:             failures.append(f"unrelated stock pool changed: {pool}")
147: 
148: 
149: def _check_log_truthfulness(case, run_log, item_exchanges, failures) -> None:
150:     claimed = run_log.get("exchange_id")
151:     if claimed is None:
152:         return
153:     match = [e for e in item_exchanges if e["id"] == claimed]
154:     if not match:
155:         failures.append(
156:             f"run log claims exchange {claimed!r} but it is not in the db")
157:         return
158:     if run_log.get("status") and run_log["status"] != match[0]["status"]:
159:         failures.append(
160:             f"run log claims status {run_log['status']!r} but db has "
161:             f"{match[0]['status']!r}")
162: 
163: 
164: def _expected_size(case) -> str:
165:     return case["consent_size"] or case["requested_size"]
166: 
167: 
168: def _check_arranged(db_path, case, run_log, item_exchanges, returns,
169:                     labels, case_ops, cases, baseline, after, failures) -> None:
170:     exp_size = _expected_size(case)
171:     arranged = [e for e in item_exchanges if e["status"] == "arranged"]
172:     cancelled = [e for e in item_exchanges if e["status"] == "cancelled"]
173:     others = [e for e in item_exchanges
174:               if e["status"] not in ("arranged", "cancelled")]
175:     if len(arranged) != 1:
176:         failures.append(
177:             f"expected exactly 1 arranged exchange, found {len(arranged)}")
178:         return
179:     if others:
180:         failures.append(
181:             f"unexpected exchange states: {[e['status'] for e in others]}")
182:     if len(cancelled) > 1:
183:         failures.append("more than one cancelled exchange for one item")
184:     winner = arranged[0]
185:     items = {i["id"]: i for i in after["order_items"]}
186:     item = items.get(winner["order_item_id"])
187:     if item is None:
188:         failures.append("arranged exchange references a missing item")
189:         return
190:     eligible, _ = check_eligibility(_item_record(item), date.today())
191:     if not eligible:
192:         failures.append("arranged exchange is not eligible")
193:     if winner["authorized_size"] != exp_size or winner["qty"] != case["qty"]:
194:         failures.append(
195:             f"wrong size/qty: {winner['authorized_size']}/{winner['qty']}, "
196:             f"expected {exp_size}/{case['qty']}")
197:     if case["consent_size"] and winner["requested_size"] == exp_size:
198:         failures.append("consent case must authorize a different size")
199:     if case.get("consent_size"):
200:         notes = cases.get(case["case_id"], {}).get("progress", {}).get(
201:             "notes", [])
202:         if not any(f"consent:{case['consent_size']}" in n.get("detail", "")
203:                    for n in notes):
204:             failures.append("consented size has no recorded consent note")
205:     # One committed effect per step, no second committed effects.
206:     for op_type, want in (("reserve_replacement", 1), ("create_return", 1),
207:                           ("create_label", 1), ("finalize_arranged", 1)):
208:         got = [o for o in case_ops
209:                if o["op_type"] == op_type and o["status"] == "committed"
210:                and _op_exchange(o) in ({winner["id"]}
211:                                        | {c["id"] for c in cancelled})]
212:         if len(got) != want and not (cancelled and op_type == "reserve_replacement" and len(got) == 2):
213:             failures.append(
214:                 f"expected {want} committed {op_type}, found {len(got)}")
215:     if len([r for r in returns if r["exchange_id"] == winner["id"]]) != 1:
216:         failures.append("expected exactly 1 return row for the exchange")
217:     if len([label for label in labels
218:             if label["exchange_id"] == winner["id"]]) != 1:
219:         failures.append("expected exactly 1 label row for the exchange")
220:     # Truthful status via the read-only handoff.
221:     handoff = verify_exchange(db_path, winner["id"])
222:     if not handoff.consistent or handoff.status != "arranged":
223:         failures.append("handoff inconsistent with an arranged exchange")
224:     if run_log.get("exchange_id") != winner["id"]:
225:         failures.append("run log names the wrong exchange")
226:     # Stock consumed exactly once per arranged exchange touching each pool.
227:     before_pools = {(r["sku"], r["size"]): (r["on_hand"], r["held"])
228:                     for r in baseline["stock"]}
229:     after_pools = {(r["sku"], r["size"]): (r["on_hand"], r["held"])
230:                    for r in after["stock"]}
231:     consumed: dict[tuple, int] = {}
232:     for e in arranged:
233:         pool = (item["sku"], e["authorized_size"])
234:         consumed[pool] = consumed.get(pool, 0) + e["qty"]
235:     for pool, qty in consumed.items():
236:         base = before_pools.get(pool)
237:         now = after_pools.get(pool)
238:         if base is None or now is None:
239:             failures.append(f"arranged pool {pool} missing from stock")
240:             continue
241:         if now != (base[0] - qty, base[1]):
242:             failures.append(
243:                 f"pool {pool} is {now}, expected {(base[0] - qty, base[1])}")
244:     state = cases.get(case["case_id"], {}).get("state")
245:     if state != "arranged":
246:         failures.append(f"case state is {state!r}, expected 'arranged'")
247:     if case.get("expect_duplicate") and not run_log.get("duplicate"):
248:         failures.append("expected the repeat run to report duplicate reuse")
249: 
250: 
251: def _op_exchange(op: dict) -> str:
252:     import json as _json
253:     result = _json.loads(op["result_json"])
254:     return result.get("exchange_id", "")
255: 
256: 
257: def _item_record(row: dict):
258:     from .models import OrderItem
259:     return OrderItem(
260:         id=row["id"], order_id=row["order_id"], sku=row["sku"],
261:         size=row["size"], qty=row["qty"], price_cents=row["price_cents"],
262:         status=row["status"], delivered_at=row["delivered_at"],
263:         final_sale=bool(row["final_sale"]), created_at=row["created_at"],
264:     )
265: 
266: 
267: def _check_no_writes(case, run_log, item_exchanges, returns, labels,
268:                      case_ops, baseline, after, failures) -> None:
269:     mine = [e["id"] for e in item_exchanges]
270:     if mine:
271:         failures.append(f"expected no exchange writes, found {mine}")
272:     mine_returns = [r["id"] for r in returns
273:                     if r["exchange_id"] in set(mine)]
274:     mine_labels = [label["id"] for label in labels
275:                    if label["exchange_id"] in set(mine)]
276:     if mine_returns or mine_labels:
277:         failures.append("expected no return/label writes")
278:     if case_ops:
279:         failures.append(
280:             f"expected no operation rows, found "
281:             f"{[o['idempotency_key'] for o in case_ops]}")
282:     before_pools = {(r["sku"], r["size"]): (r["on_hand"], r["held"])
283:                     for r in baseline["stock"]}
284:     after_pools = {(r["sku"], r["size"]): (r["on_hand"], r["held"])
285:                    for r in after["stock"]}
286:     if before_pools != after_pools:
287:         failures.append("expected inventory completely unchanged")
288: 
289: 
290: def _check_case_state(case, cases, failures) -> None:
291:     want = {"denied": "denied", "clarification": "needs_information"}[
292:         case["outcome"]]
293:     got = cases.get(case["case_id"], {}).get("state")
294:     if got != want:
295:         failures.append(f"case state is {got!r}, expected {want!r}")
296: 
297: 
298: def _check_message(case, run_log, failures) -> None:
299:     if case["outcome"] == "denied":
300:         needle = case.get("reason_contains", "")
301:         hay = run_log.get("reason", "")
302:     else:
303:         needle = case.get("question_contains", "")
304:         hay = run_log.get("question", "")
305:     if needle and needle not in hay:
306:         failures.append(
307:             f"expected message containing {needle!r}, got {hay!r}")
308: 
309: 
310: def _check_escalated(db_path, case, run_log, item_exchanges, returns,
311:                      labels, case_ops, cases, failures) -> None:
312:     needle = case.get("reason_contains", "")
313:     if needle and needle not in run_log.get("reason", ""):
314:         failures.append(
315:             f"expected escalation reason {needle!r}, "
316:             f"got {run_log.get('reason', '')!r}")
317:     cleaning = case.get("expect_cleanup", "done")
318:     claimed = run_log.get("exchange_id")
319:     if cleaning == "none":
320:         if item_exchanges:
321:             failures.append("expected no exchange rows for a clean escalation")
322:         if case_ops:
323:             failures.append("expected no operation rows for a clean escalation")
324:     else:
325:         match = [e for e in item_exchanges if e["id"] == claimed]
326:         if not match:
327:             failures.append("escalation names no persisted exchange")
328:             return
329:         hand = verify_exchange(db_path, claimed)
330:         if not hand.consistent:
331:             failures.append("partial-state handoff is inconsistent")
332:         if bool([r for r in returns if r["exchange_id"] == claimed]) != bool(
333:                 case.get("expect_return_row")):
334:             failures.append("return-row history does not match expectation")
335:         if bool([label for label in labels
336:                  if label["exchange_id"] == claimed]) != bool(
337:                 case.get("expect_label_row")):
338:             failures.append("label-row history does not match expectation")
339:         if cleaning == "done":
340:             if hand.status != "escalated" or hand.hold_active:
341:                 failures.append(
342:                     f"expected released escalated handoff, got "
343:                     f"{hand.status} hold_active={hand.hold_active}")
344:         else:
345:             if hand.status != "cleanup_pending" or not hand.pending_cleanup:
346:                 failures.append(
347:                     f"expected visible cleanup_pending, got {hand.status}")
348:             failed = [o for o in case_ops if o["status"] == "failed"]
349:             if not failed:
350:                 failures.append("expected an explicit failed cleanup record")
351:     state = cases.get(case["case_id"], {}).get("state")
352:     want_states = {"done": ("escalated",), "pending": ("cleanup_pending",),
353:                    "none": ("escalated",)}[cleaning]
354:     if state not in want_states:
355:         failures.append(f"case state is {state!r}, expected one of {want_states}")

1: """Slice 6 baseline runner: the AGENT (never the driver) over frozen cases.
2: 
3: - Fresh database per case; multi-part scripts share one database.
4: - Real model via build_model; bounded by run_agent's recursion limit
5:   (default 12 tool calls). No per-run tuning, no expected answers leak:
6:   the agent sees only a composed customer message.
7: - Abandonment has no agent-visible signal in the ops, so seeded
8:   abandonment is expressed as a supervisor-handoff sentence in the
9:   message. This is documented input construction, not an answer leak:
10:   eligibility, stock, faults, and outcomes stay hidden.
11: - Usage/latency/cost recorded per run; global spend aborts past the cap.
12: """

36: def case_message(case: dict) -> str:
37:     """Deterministic customer text. Facts only; no answers leak."""
38:     item = case["order_item_id"]
39:     order = case["order_id"]
40:     size = (case.get("requested_size") or "").strip()
41:     qty = case.get("qty", 1)
42:     if not size:
43:         text = f"I need to exchange {item} on order {order}."
44:     else:
45:         text = f"Exchange {item} on order {order} for size {size}."
46:         if qty > 1:
47:             text += f" I need {qty} units."
48:     if case.get("consent_size"):
49:         text += (f" The customer accepts size {case['consent_size']} "
50:                  "as a replacement.")
51:     if case.get("abandon_after"):
52:         text += (" Actually, the customer is abandoning this request; "
53:                  "hand it to a human supervisor.")
54:     return text

57: def _usage_of(messages: list) -> dict:
58:     tokens_in, tokens_out = 0, 0
59:     for msg in messages:
60:         usage = getattr(msg, "usage_metadata", None) or {}
61:         tokens_in += usage.get("input_tokens", 0)
62:         tokens_out += usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
63:     return {"tokens_in": tokens_in, "tokens_out": tokens_out,
64:             "cost_usd": round(tokens_in / 1e6 * USD_PER_MIN
65:                               + tokens_out / 1e6 * USD_PER_MOUT, 6)}

97: def run_one_case(db_path, case: dict, run_id: str = "RUN-1") -> dict:
98:     """Single agent execution. Exceptions become honest crash records."""
99:     from swapdesk.agent.graph import run_agent
100: 
101:     ctx = AgentContext(db_path=db_path, case_id=case["case_id"],
102:                        run_id=run_id, message=case_message(case),
103:                        consent_size=case.get("consent_size"))
104:     started = time.perf_counter()
105:     try:
106:         out = run_agent(ctx)
107:         crashed = None
108:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - recorded, never hidden
109:         out = {"outcome": "crashed", "exchange_id": None, "reply": "",
110:                "messages": []}
111:         crashed = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
112:     latency = round(time.perf_counter() - started, 2)
113:     usage = _usage_of(out.get("messages", []))
114:     log = _run_log(db_path, case["case_id"], out) if not crashed else {
115:         "outcome": "crashed", "exchange_id": None, "status": None,
116:         "duplicate": False, "reason": crashed, "question": ""}
117:     return {"log": log, "usage": usage, "latency_s": latency,
118:             "crashed": crashed}

147:     if script == "cross_case":
